newsitem.title: MALI: Mali reschedules parliamentary poll again.
newsitem.headline: Mali reschedules parliamentary poll again.

text.p: Mali's government announced new dates for rerunning the West African nation's scrapped parliamentary elections, postponing the polls for a further two weeks.
A statement issued after a special cabinet meeting on Friday said the two rounds of the elections would now be held on July 20 and August 3.

The constitutional court ruled in April that numerous irregularities had flawed the April 13 first round vote for the former French colony's 147-seat parliament. The government had previously set the rerun for July 6 and 20.
Main opposition parties later boycotted presidential elections on May 11 in which incumbent Alpha Oumar Konare won 84.36 percent of the votes in the first round.

Five opposition leaders, detained after protests over Konare's reelection, were among about 10 people convicted on Tuesday on charges of refusing to recognise the authority of the state, destruction of public and private property and inciting violence.

The opposition has made any dialogue with Konare conditional on the release of the five -- Mountaga Tall of the National Congress for Democratic Initiative (CNID), Almamy Sylla of the Rally for Democracy and Progress (RDP), Sogal Maiga of the Patriotic Movement for Renewal (MPR), Colonel Issouf Traore of the Union of Democratic and Popular Forces (UFDP) and youth leader Moussa Kone.

Mali had been widely praised for its 1992 transition from Moussa Traore's dictatorship to a multi-party system. Military leader Amadou Toumani Toure stepped down after 14 months and now often mediates in regional political crises.
